primary_math: Let x=DB and y=AC. Triangle ADB has sides7,2,x:5<x<9. Triangle DCB has3,4,x:1<x<7. Thus integer x=6. Triangle ABC has2,4,y:2<y<6. Triangle ADC has7,3,y:4<y<10. Thus integer y=5. The sum is11 uniquely. The frozen source coordinates realize these lengths in a nondegenerate tetrahedron (D has nonzero z, A/B/C lie in z=0). A blue edge correspondence cannot transfer the explicit4 on CB to AC; the original4 remains next to CB. No equality tick or textual equality is added.
